News / Benzinga / Mike Johnson Calls for 'Investment,' Not Probe, After FAA Ground Stop as Duffy's $50 Billion Ask Draws Fire From Greene

Mike Johnson Calls for 'Investment,' Not Probe, After FAA Ground Stop as Duffy's $50 Billion Ask Draws Fire From Greene 2 min read

LHX House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said Saturday that Congress doesn’t need to investigate Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop, but it does need to fund upgrades. "We don’t really need any investigation … we need further investment," Johnson said on Fox News’ "Saturday in America." He noted that some equipment dates to the 1980s.

Saturday in America @SatAmericaFNC

🚨SPEAKER MIKE JOHNSON SAYS HOUSE IS WORKING ON FAA FUNDING AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP @SpeakerJohnson tells @KayleighMcEnany he’s in Washington this weekend working on legislation to modernize America’s air traffic control system. "We’re going to work to get it done."⬇️… pic.twitter.com/V6Dms1cNqO

Nov 14, 2026

Router Fault Under Review Government officials said Saturday a single router installed by L3Harris Technologies Inc. LHX may have caused the outage, Reuters reported. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cause remains undetermined. Duffy said Friday the contractor was switching lines from copper wire to fiber. In a statement, L3Harris said it has completed more than 70% of that conversion and is supporting the FAA’s investigation. Duffy said the new routers flooded others with over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. The routers being replaced are about 25 years old, Duffy said, and were due for replacement in 2006. Rare Stoppage Disrupts Air Travel The FAA issued the ground stop around 4 p.m. EST Friday. Duffy said it was lifted around 8:15 p.m. The agency’s last widespread stoppage lasted about 90 minutes in January 2023 . As of 9:25 p.m. EST Saturday, FlightAware data showed 8,048 delays and 6,445 cancellations within, into or out of the U.S. $50 Billion Funding Push On Friday, Duffy called the system "incredibly old" and said, "I want $50 billion." Congress has already given the FAA $12.5 billion for upgrades. In a Saturday post on X, Duffy called modernization a " national safety priority ." He said Congress needs to step up with resources to build a "state-of-the-art system." Greene And Torres Question Aviation Funding Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-Ga.) criticized the $50 billion funding request . In a long post on X on Saturday, she said she was "blown away" by people who "fell for the total garbage" at Friday’s press conference, and said officials lied about what happened. She said the systems need updating and "it takes money," but that officials have "plenty of money."

Marjorie Taylor Greene 🇺🇸 @mtgreenee

Rep. Norma Torres (D-Calif.) wrote on X, "Before asking taxpayers for more, this administration owes answers about how existing funds are being spent and why our aviation system is still falling behind."

Sean Duffy wants $50 billion to fix our air traffic control system. But Congress already provided $12.5 billion for FAA modernization, and DOT and OMB have requested another $30.1 billion. item.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX Faces Fresh Zelenskyy Backlash Over 161 Kph Starshield Speed Cap
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday renewed criticism of Elon Musk-led Space Exploration Technologies Corp. NASDAQ:SPCX over speed caps of 161 kph on its Starshield military terminals ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / Elon Musk’s SpaceX Faces Fresh Zelenskyy Backlash Over 161 Kph Starshield Speed Cap

Elon Musk’s SpaceX Faces Fresh Zelenskyy Backlash Over 161 Kph Starshield Speed Cap 1 min read

SPCX Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday renewed criticism of Elon Musk -led Space Exploration Technologies Corp. SPCX over speed caps of 161 kph on its Starshield military terminals in occupied territory, hampering air defenses against Russian drones. According to remarks his office released, Zelenskyy said the limit has been in place for five days. He said it makes it harder to intercept jet-powered Russian drones and leaves cities more exposed. Zelenskyy Warns of Political Fallout From Starshield Limits Zelenskyy also warned that keeping restrictions in occupied areas while lifting them elsewhere in Ukraine was extremely dangerous. He said it carried political implications and implied partial non-recognition of those territories as Ukrainian. He rejected the explanation that the cap is a technical glitch. "We do not believe that is the case," he told reporters. He said he ordered his top military and foreign ministry officials to address the issue and seek clarification. SpaceX denied adding restrictions or altering satellite operations, Reuters reported. SpaceX did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments. Second Speed Dispute in Weeks It is the second such dispute in recent weeks. In mid-October, Ukrainian officials said SpaceX capped Starlink and Starshield speeds at about 160 kph . That followed a sharp turn in U.S.-Ukraine relations. President Donald Trump said Ukraine should get "a new president," a day after announcing a deal to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports . Service was restored Oct. 24. Musk said on X that Ukraine’s military violated Starlink’s terms of service . Using Starlink, "a civilian commercial service," for offensive drone strikes "has never been allowed," he said. The latest disruption follows renewed escalation between Russia and Ukraine, a day after Abu Dhabi talks. SpaceX has a market capitalization of about $1.89 trillion. Over the past 52 weeks, its stock has traded as high as $225.64 and as low as $104.83. News / ACCESS Newswire / New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and Fr…

New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and FreeCast 7 min read

AIIO AMFN CAST SWRD Jane King hosts conversations on sovereign AI, fusion energy, global private credit and partner-led streaming infrastructure, airing at 6:30 p.m. ET across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 14, 2026 / AI is driving record spending on data centers, and with it, soaring costs for storage, bandwidth and power. Fusion developers are racing to deliver clean, around-the-clock energy. International investors are looking for returns that don't move with the rest of their portfolios. And companies that already own the customer relationship want to own the screen, too. Tonight, New to The Street brings leaders working on each of those challenges to a global business audience as Show #780 premieres at 6:30 p.m. ET on Bloomberg Television as sponsored programming, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and Southeast Asia. Hosted by Jane King, Show #780 features executive conversations with: Ralf R. Debbas , President of Robo.ai Inc. AIIO Dr. Jasem Al Mansoori , Chief Executive Officer of ALIF Holding Mansoor Ali Khan , Chief Technology Officer of Neurovia AI Brent Nelson , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Fusion Inc. AMFN Bilal Adam , Chief Executive Officer of Stewards Investment Capital William "Bill" Mobley , Founder and Chief Executive Officer of FreeCast, Inc. CAST "Show #780 is about the infrastructure behind the next economy," said Vince Caruso, Co-Founder and CEO of New to The Street. "A UAE-based, Nasdaq-listed group building sovereign AI and industrial capability. A fusion company opening its technology to independent review. An investment firm connecting emerging and developed markets. And a software company turning every internet connection into a media business. These are the stories our audience in every region tunes in for. No politics. No current events. Only Opportunities To Consider™." INSIDE SHOW #780 Robo.ai Inc. AIIO : Where Global AI Investment Meets Local Capability In a three-executive panel, Jane King asks where Robo.ai fits in the AI investment cycle. Ralf R. Debbas, President of Robo.ai, describes the company as a UAE-based, Nasdaq-listed group "connecting regional technology with global market reach." He outlines its main operating businesses: Neurovia AI, focused on visual data efficiency; ALIF Holding, which brings industrial integration, manufacturing and execution; and Quantum Core Capital (QC Capital), which contributes operating revenue and is developing AI applications including AI-generated video and content creation. "Our ambition is to help build sovereign AI capabilities within the UAE itself and the wider region," Debbas said, "technology that can be deployed, supported and developed locally." Dr. Jasem Al Mansoori, Chief Executive Officer of ALIF Holding, Robo.ai's Abu Dhabi-based industrial group, draws on more than 30 years at the UAE Ministry of Interior. "This experience taught me the importance of reliable solutions and strong local support," he said. ALIF is developing an industrial base in the UAE for engineering and manufacturing, and aims to use AI to help industrial customers work more efficiently and make better decisions. Mansoor Ali Khan, Chief Technology Officer of Neurovia AI, explains why efficiency matters as AI computing competition intensifies and memory and storage costs rise. Khan notes that the large majority of the world's data is visual and unstructured. Neurovia's flagship NeuroStream™ platform is designed to reduce the volume of visual data that is transmitted, processed and stored. In a company demonstration shown on air, a 12.15 GB 4K video file was reduced to 421 MB, a reduction of more than 96%. Khan said the goal is to address the main costs of AI (storage, compute, transmission and power) and make AI "more affordable and sustainable." Actual results depend on deployment conditions and use-case validation. Learn more at roboai.group. American Fusion Inc. AMFN : Independent Review, a New Texas Campus and a Busy Six Months Chairman and CEO Brent Nelson returns to update Jane King on American Fusion's Texatron™ aneutronic fusion engine. Nelson says an independent third-party reviewer recently completed an on-site evaluation of the technology, with a final report expected later this month. "The draft highlights look good so far," he said, adding that the company hopes the report will confirm "that we're on the right track." Nelson, who added the CEO title in late October, says his priorities for the next six months include closing on the company's North Texas "Ranch" facility, which American Fusion expects by Thanksgiving, and developing the property. The company is also moving from its temporary facility into new lab and office space, and plans to build its own testing bunker at the Ranch. "We're still operating and testing the Texatron on a daily basis," Nelson said, "and our data is getting better." He also says the company's patent program remains active, with new applications being written daily, and that its data center proposals are moving forward. Learn more at americanfusionenergy.com. Stewards Investment Capital CEO Bilal Adam on Global Investing, Private Credit and Financial Inclusion Bilal Adam, Chief Executive Officer of Stewards Investment Capital, joins Jane King to discuss the firm's international investment approach, private credit solutions and commitment to financial inclusion. A chartered accountant from South Africa with a background in investment banking, Adam describes building a business with activities spanning South Africa, Mauritius, the United States and Monaco. Adam discusses the firm's investment philosophy, which he says starts with "aiming to do good first," and its relationship with Nasdaq-listed Stewards, Inc. SWRD , a U.S.-based diversified financial platform led by President and CEO Shaun Quin, which provides financing to small businesses across the United States. Stewards Investment Capital is affiliated with, but separate from, Stewards, Inc. He also highlights telecommunications tower investments aimed at expanding connectivity and financial inclusion in rural African communities. The conversation explores how Stewards Investment Capital provides pension funds, institutions, family offices and high-net-worth investors with access to private credit, portfolio diversification and international investment opportunities, including a private credit approach that funds fractional amounts of loans to small businesses. Learn more at stewardsinvestment.com. FreeCast, Inc. CAST : "The Connection Is Just the Beginning" Founder and CEO William Mobley explains why FreeCast is "not another streaming service." Instead, the company provides the software infrastructure that lets telecom companies, wireless carriers, internet providers, satellite companies and membership organizations launch their own branded entertainment hubs, offering free television, premium subscriptions, sports, advertising and commerce. "They bring the customers," Mobley said. "We bring the media and monetization technology." Mobley walks through PEAC, FreeCast's metric for "partner-enabled addressable customers," which measures potential distribution reach through enterprise agreements. He is clear that PEAC does not represent active users, paying subscribers or confirmed revenue. He describes the company's job as converting that reach into activated users, transactions and, ultimately, revenue across advertising, subscriptions, pay-per-view, live sports, rentals and commerce. "We don't need Netflix to lose for FreeCast to succeed," Mobley said. "We want more content and more services participating in our marketplaces." Learn more at freecast.com. FEATURED COMMERCIALS SafeSpace Global Corporation SSGC : An AI-powered safety and security platform designed to help protect the vulnerable in schools, senior care, addiction treatment, correctional facilities and houses of worship. "Smarter technology, faster response, safer spaces." T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA : Completed a strategic refinancing of its Orofino, Idaho data center and added a new appointment to its board of directors. Big Sky Industrial BSIN : Advancing helium production, carbon management and strategic energy infrastructure through its flagship Big Sky Carbon Hub, targeting demand from AI, semiconductors, healthcare and aerospace. Acurx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ACXP : Developing what could be the first new class of antibiotics in nearly 40 years, with the FDA agreeing to consider a future application for lead drug ibezapolstat based on two planned trials, Pathfinder and Aspire. HOW TO WATCH Bloomberg Television: Tonight, Saturday, November 14, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. ET, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia New to The Street TV on YouTube (5.44M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewtoTheStreetTV NewsOut on YouTube (1.24M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewsOutChannel Following the broadcast, every segment will be distributed across the New to The Street TV and NewsOut YouTube channels, which together have more than 6.6 million subscribers. MEET THE COMPANIES 2027: NEW YORK, ATLANTIC CITY AND LAS VEGAS New to The Street's Meet The Companies tour brings presenting companies face to face with family offices, accredited investors and high-net-worth individuals in three cities in 2027. Every presentation is filmed and distributed across New to The Street's U.S., Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia platforms and its 6.6M+ subscriber YouTube network, so each company reaches a guaranteed audience well beyond the room. No vendor pitches. New York - Thursday, January 7, 2027: The Hudson Yards Penthouse, 455 Tenth Avenue PH, New York, NY 10018, the week before the Needham Growth Conference, with a cocktail reception on Wednesday, January 6 Atlantic City - Thursday, January 28, 2027 Las Vegas - June 17-18, 2027 Each event hosts up to 20 presenting companies, with 20-minute slots that include a 15-minute presentation and Q&A. For Atlantic City and Las Vegas presenters, New to The Street pays for your stay. Confirmed New York Presenters Glint (glintpay.com) TMC the metals company Inc. TMC American Fusion Inc. AMFN Big Sky Industrial BSIN T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA Stewards, Inc. SWRD Roadzen Inc. RDZN Smile Design Manhattan Additional presenters will be announced. Accredited investors only. Apply to attend: John@NewtoTheStreet.com. Companies interested in a presenting slot can contact John Battenfield at John@NewtoTheStreet.com. ABOUT NEW TO THE STREET Founded in 2009, New to The Street is a sponsored and syndicated business television platform serving public companies, emerging-growth businesses and companies preparing to enter the public markets. Co-founded and led by CEO Vince Caruso, New to The Street combines weekly Bloomberg Television broadcasts across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia with long-form executive interviews, television commercials, earned media, social-media distribution, NewsOut video press-release coverage, accredited-investor events and premium outdoor advertising, including Times Square billboards. The platform has worked with more than 200 public companies. No politics. No current events. Only Opportunities To Consider™. SOURCE: New to The Street
